title: else if ladders
learningGoals: chain several tests with else if
order the tests from strict to loose
use a final else for all other cases

youtube.title: C++ else if Ladder: Grades and Choices | C++ Programming EP 14
youtube.description: In this episode you will chain several tests with else if, order the tests from strict to loose and use a final else for all other cases, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 else if ladders · 0:46 A grade ladder · 1:26 Grade bands · 1:56 Second program · 2:56 Recap · 3:26 Bug of the Day · 4:14 Challenge · 4:34 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "THE LADDER" in tomato on cream; Xecxec next to a ladder with a grade letter on each rung; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a ladder with a grade letter on each rung

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we handle more than two cases. We build a grade calculator with an else if ladder.

scenes.onScreen: "else if ladders": numbered lines (1. Tests run from the top down; 2. The first true test wins; 3. The last else catches everything else) and an analogy card: a ladder: you climb down until a rung fits
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: An else if ladder checks tests from the top down. The first true test runs, and the rest are skipped. A final else catches all other cases. The order matters. Put the strictest test first. Think of a ladder. You climb down from the top until you find a rung that fits.
points: Tests run from the top down
The last else catches everything else

analogy.title: else if ladders
analogy.body: A ladder: you climb down until a rung fits

scenes.onScreen: grade.cpp: an else if ladder turns marks into a grade
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] Marks is eighty-two. [HL 6] Is it at least ninety? No, so we move down. [HL 8] Is it at least seventy-five? Yes. [HL 9] This branch prints Grade B. The ladder stops here. [HL 10] The tests below never run. [HL 12] The last else would catch every mark below fifty.

scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: This table shows the bands. Each test only needs the lower limit. The tests above it have already removed the higher marks. That is why order is so important.

scenes.onScreen: ticket.cpp: the age picks the ticket price
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 5] The age is sixty-five. [HL 7] Under five is free. [HL 9] Under eighteen pays fifty. [HL 11] Under sixty pays one hundred. [HL 13] Everyone else gets the senior price of sixty. [TRACK price=60] Sixty-five matches the else branch. [HL 16] The program prints the price.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as ticket dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Price colon sixty.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. An else if ladder checks tests from the top down. Two. The first true test runs, and the rest are skipped. Three. Put the strictest test first. Four. A final else catches every other case. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: An else if ladder checks tests from the top down.
The first true test runs, and the rest are skipped.
A final else catches every other case.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: Tests in the wrong order
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the program runs and the wrong output appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the output turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. A student has eighty-two marks. The program prints Pass, not Distinction. The loose test is first, and eighty-two passes it. The ladder stops there. Always put the strictest test first. Then the ladder works from the top down.

scenes.onScreen: I built a ladder of else ifs. Now I cannot find the right rung to get down.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I built a ladder of else ifs. Now I cannot find the right rung to get down.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: write a ladder for temperature
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write an else if ladder for a temperature. Print hot above thirty-five, warm above twenty-five, and cool for the rest. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: switch and case. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Program output (it runs, but the answer is wrong):

Pass
bug.why: Eighty-two passes the first test, so the ladder stops. The strict test below never gets a turn.

pun: "I built a ladder of else ifs. Now I cannot find the right rung to get down."
challenge: Write an else if ladder for a temperature. Print hot above thirty-five, warm above twenty-five, and cool for the rest.
challengeAnswer: Test temperature greater than thirty-five first. Then test greater than twenty-five. End with an else that prints cool.
